title: Tungnath & Chandrashila
summary: The highest Shiva temple in the world, and a short climb on to Chandrashila for a sunrise over Chaukhamba, Nanda Devi and Trishul.

itinerary.x: Meet in Rishikesh in the morning. Drive about 200 km via Devprayag, Rudraprayag and Ukhimath. Stay in Chopta's camps or homestays.
Start before dawn, reach Tungnath (3.5 km), continue 1.5 km to Chandrashila for sunrise, then come down for darshan. Rest in Chopta.
Drive back, reaching Rishikesh by evening.

tips: Leave Chopta by 4:30 am if you want the Chandrashila sunrise.
In winter the temple closes and the deity moves to Makkumath.

title: Kedarnath
summary: The first and most visited of the Panch Kedar, set under the Kedarnath peaks at the head of the Mandakini valley.

itinerary.x: Long drive along the Alaknanda and Mandakini. Stay in Sonprayag or Guptkashi.
Shared jeep to Gaurikund, then the 16 km trail up. Evening aarti at the temple.
Early darshan, walk up to Bhairavnath temple, then trek back to Gaurikund. Stay in Sonprayag.
Drive back, reaching Rishikesh by evening.

tips: Register online for the Char Dham yatra before you travel (registrationandtouristcare.uk.gov.in). It is checked at the shrine.
Start the trek early; afternoons often bring rain and crowded trails.
Phones and cameras are not allowed inside the temple premises, so film outside.

title: Rudranath
summary: The toughest of the Panch Kedar: long climbs through oak forest and wide alpine meadows to a cave shrine where Shiva is worshipped as a face.

itinerary.x: Drive to Gopeshwar near Chamoli and rest.
Steep climb through forest to the Panar meadows. Overnight in a basic hut or tent.
Ridge walk past Pitradhar with big views of Nanda Devi and Trishul. Evening darshan.
Long descent the same way. Stay in Gopeshwar.
Drive back, reaching Rishikesh by evening.

tips: Few shops on this route, so carry snacks and water purification.
Hire a local guide or porter from Sagar if it is your first high-altitude trek.

title: Madhyamaheshwar
summary: A quiet green trail through villages and forest to the temple of Shiva's navel, with Chaukhamba right above the meadow.

itinerary.x: Drive via Rudraprayag and Ukhimath to the roadhead at Ransi.
Down to Gaundar village, then a steady climb to the temple meadow.
Walk about 2 km up to Budha Madhyamaheshwar for Chaukhamba views, then trek down to Ransi.
Drive back, reaching Rishikesh by evening.

tips: Homestays at Gaundar and near the temple are simple; book ahead in peak season.

title: Kalpeshwar
summary: The fifth Kedar, a rock-cave shrine in the Urgam valley where Shiva's matted hair is worshipped. The only Panch Kedar open all year.

itinerary.x: Drive up the Alaknanda to Helang, then turn into the Urgam valley. Stay in a village homestay.
Short walk from Devgram to the cave temple. Spend the rest of the day in the valley.
Drive back, reaching Rishikesh by evening.

tips: Easy to add to a Badrinath or Valley of Flowers trip since Helang is on the same highway.

title: Badrinath & Mana
summary: The Char Dham shrine of Vishnu on the Alaknanda between the Nar and Narayan ranges, with Mana village a few kilometres on.

itinerary.x: Drive past the five prayags along the Alaknanda.
Dip in Tapt Kund, darshan, then Mana village, Bhim Pul and the Saraswati river. Stay in Joshimath.
Drive back, reaching Rishikesh by evening.

tips: Register online for the Char Dham yatra before you travel (registrationandtouristcare.uk.gov.in). It is checked at the shrine.
Phones and cameras are not allowed inside the temple premises, so film outside.

title: Auli & Gorson Bugyal
summary: Snow slopes in winter and open meadows in summer, with a walk up to Gorson Bugyal and Nanda Devi across the valley.

itinerary.x: Drive up the Alaknanda via Rudraprayag and Chamoli to Joshimath, then the last stretch up to Auli.
Walk about 3 km through oak and conifer forest to the Gorson Bugyal meadow for views of Nanda Devi and Dronagiri. Back in Auli by afternoon.
Drive back, reaching Rishikesh by evening.

tips: Come in January or February for snow; ski gear can be hired in Auli.
Easy to pair with Badrinath or Valley of Flowers, which are on the same highway past Joshimath.

title: Valley of Flowers
route: Rishikesh → Govindghat → Ghangaria → Valley of Flowers
summary: A UNESCO-listed alpine valley that turns into a carpet of wildflowers in the monsoon, with Hemkund Sahib as an optional climb.

itinerary.x: Drive to Govindghat near Joshimath.
Shared jeep to Pulna, then about 10 km up the Lakshman Ganga to Ghangaria.
Walk into the valley (about 4 km in) and spend the day among the flowers. Return to Ghangaria by evening.
Trek back to Pulna. Add a day here if you want the steep climb to Hemkund Sahib.
Drive back, reaching Rishikesh by evening.

tips: The park is open 1 June to 31 October. Entry is 7 am to 2 pm and everyone must be out by 5 pm.
The permit (about ₹150 for Indians, valid three days) is available online or at the forest counter in Ghangaria. Camping inside is not allowed.
Pack a proper rain jacket; this is a monsoon trek.

title: Kartik Swami
summary: A ridge-top temple to Lord Kartikeya, rare in North India, with a 360° view of the Kedar and Chaukhamba ranges at sunset.

itinerary.x: Drive to Kanakchauri via Rudraprayag, then the 3 km climb to the temple for sunset and evening aarti. Stay in Kanakchauri.
Drive back, reaching Rishikesh by evening.

tips: Go for the evening aarti and sunset, but carry a torch for the walk down.

title: Harshil Valley
summary: A deodar-and-apple valley on the Bhagirathi, with Bagori village and Mukhba, the winter home of Goddess Ganga.

itinerary.x: Drive via Uttarkashi up the Bhagirathi valley and settle into a riverside stay.
Walk through Bagori village and the orchards, then visit Mukhba across the river.
Drive back, reaching Rishikesh by evening.

tips: Pair it with Gangotri, which is only about an hour further up the road.

title: Gangotri
summary: The Char Dham shrine of Goddess Ganga where the Bhagirathi runs through a granite gorge. Gaumukh glacier is an optional permit trek.

itinerary.x: Drive up the Bhagirathi valley and stay in Uttarkashi.
Drive past Harshil to Gangotri. Evening aarti on the Bhagirathi ghats.

itinerary.t: Surya Kund and back to Uttarkashi
itinerary.x: Darshan, Surya Kund falls and the Bhagirath Shila, then drive down to Uttarkashi.
Drive back, reaching Rishikesh by evening.

tips: Register online for the Char Dham yatra before you travel (registrationandtouristcare.uk.gov.in). It is checked at the shrine.
Gaumukh needs a forest permit with a daily quota; apply early.
Phones and cameras are not allowed inside the temple premises, so film outside.

title: Yamunotri
summary: The first of the Char Dham, the temple of Goddess Yamuna below Bandarpunch, reached by a steep 6 km walk from Janki Chatti.

itinerary.x: Drive via Mussoorie or Chamba to Barkot on the Yamuna. Stay in Barkot.
Drive to Janki Chatti and walk 6 km up to the temple. Dip in the hot springs, see Surya Kund and Divya Shila, then walk back down and return to Barkot.
Drive back, reaching Rishikesh by evening.

tips: Register online for the Char Dham yatra before you travel (registrationandtouristcare.uk.gov.in). It is checked at the shrine.
The trail is short but steep; ponies and palkis are available at Janki Chatti if you need them.
Phones and cameras are not allowed inside the temple premises, so film outside.

title: Brahmatal Trek
summary: A classic winter snow trek through oak and rhododendron forest to two frozen lakes, with Trishul and Nanda Ghunti right in front of you.

itinerary.x: Long drive via Karnaprayag and Tharali to Lohajung, the trek's base village.
Climb through oak and rhododendron forest to camp near Bekaltal lake.
Walk the ridge past Tilandi to the Brahmatal lake campsite.
Early climb to Brahmatal top (about 3,734 m) for Trishul and Nanda Ghunti, then come down to the lower camp.
Descend through the forest to Lohajung.
Drive back, reaching Rishikesh by late evening.

tips: In peak winter the lakes freeze and snow covers the trail; carry gaiters and microspikes.
Go with a registered local trek organiser or guide; campsites have no permanent shelter.

title: Kuari Pass Trek
route: Rishikesh → Joshimath → Dhak → Kuari Pass → Auli
summary: Lord Curzon's old trail through meadows and forest to a pass facing Nanda Devi, Dronagiri, Kamet and Hathi Ghoda in one sweep.

itinerary.x: Drive up the Alaknanda past the five prayags to Joshimath.
Short drive to Dhak, then climb through villages and forest to the Gulling campsite.
Walk through oak forest to the Khullara meadows.
Climb to the pass (about 3,815 m) for the full Garhwal panorama, then return to camp.
Descend via Tali through the forest to Auli, then on to Joshimath.
Drive back, reaching Rishikesh by evening.

tips: Winter brings snow from about Khullara upwards; summer turns the meadows green.
Combine with a day in Auli or a visit to Badrinath if you have extra days.

title: Satopanth Tal Trek
summary: A tough high-altitude walk from Mana along the Alaknanda's glacier valley to a triangular sacred lake under Chaukhamba and Neelkanth.

itinerary.x: Drive up the Alaknanda valley to Joshimath.
Short drive to Badrinath. Darshan, then rest and acclimatise.
Walk from Mana past Vasudhara falls to the Laxmi Van campsite.
Cross moraine and boulder fields past Sahastradhara to Chakratirtha.
Steep climb to the lake (about 4,600 m) under Chaukhamba, then back to Chakratirtha.
Long walk down to Mana and Badrinath.
Long drive back, reaching Rishikesh late in the evening.

tips: This trek is above 4,000 m on unmarked moraine; do it only with prior high-altitude experience.
Check permit rules with the forest office in Joshimath or Badrinath before you go, and take a registered local guide.
Nights at Chakratirtha are below freezing even in summer; carry a proper sleeping bag.
